correctness.rationale: For viable sizes a=q−j, b=q+j the original-degree restriction is nI−A(K_{a,b}). If both parts are nonempty the all-ones directions give a two-by-two block with diagonal n and off-diagonal −√(ab); the within-part zero-sum vectors have eigenvalue n. If one part is empty the restriction is nI. This proves λ=n−√(q²−j²) and both extrema by strict monotonicity in |j| over its feasible range. The allocation law follows by counting uniformly drawn fixed-cardinality subsets; the hypergeometric variance is mq/(2n−1). The CLT applies because sample and complement sizes are both proportional to n and the success fraction is 1/2. Rationalizing the spectral deficit gives X=λ−m=J²/(q+√(q²−J²)); the denominator is 2q(1+o_P(1)). Therefore X converges to (ρ/4)Z². Hoeffding's bound for sampling without replacement gives P(|J|>t)≤2exp(−t²/m), so X≤J²/q has uniformly bounded moments of order larger than two when q is proportional to n. This proves the claimed mean and variance limits. The nonlinear test is strict: a positive principal vector φ gives H′≤(r−Dλ)H−rH²/∑φ, including equality and the case nI. Above threshold εφ and large constants give ordered positive sub- and supersolutions of the cooperative ODE. If two positive equilibria differed, scaling one by θ>1 until first touch with the other yields f_i(u)≤f_i(θv)=−rθ(θ−1)v_i²<0 at a touching coordinate, contradicting equilibrium. Monotone comparison then gives attraction for strictly positive initial data. The event X<c is therefore exactly persistence, yielding the stated error-function limit for c>0 and zero at c≤0. These steps verify RESULT.md lines 48–112 analytically. The packaged finite checker is supplementary and was not executed.

value.rationale: At the same fixed sink budget the comparison identifies a precise order-one random penalty relative to optimal allocation, while the worst placement costs order n at positive limiting sink fraction. The non-Gaussian distribution quantifies the actual persistence probability when the growth-to-diffusion ratio is tuned within O(1) of the best threshold, where first-order concentration supplies no answer. It is a useful structured-habitat benchmark without claiming the same window for general graphs.
